Decision rule derived from the measured deltas (1.7 points at 50 facts vs 10.0 at 800) plus the query-shape distinction built into the fixture (cluster-level vs exact-paraphrase). It is advice scoped to those measurements, not a general guarantee.

Operational consequence of the measured prefix-truncation semantics: a short vector is derivable from a stored full-width vector without a second embed call, so a two-width index plus full-width rescoring is implementable. title_options: Ollama dimensions for Agent Memory: What Cutting Vector Width Costs in Recall
Agent Memory Vector Truncation: The Recall Cost Grows With the Index

presentation.title_rationale: Selected title fronts the product surface the reader searched for (ollama dimensions) and the object it changes (agent memory vectors), then promises one supported consequence: a measured recall cost. 'What ... Costs in Recall' is exactly what the curve reports (1.7 points R@5 at a 50-fact index, 10.0 points at 800 facts) and carries no universal claim - the fixture scale, host and ollama 0.20.3 pin are stated in the first section and in Limits. 77 characters, so no long_title_reason is needed; the year suffix was dropped from the headline because it described the supply period, not the finding.
presentation.visual_purpose: Shows the article's central interaction: recall@5 against stored vector width (384, 256, 128, 64 dims, with float32 bytes per vector) for three index sizes of the same 800-fact corpus. The three lines are plotted directly from summary-arctic-presence-guaranteed.json 3-seed means, so the reader sees that the 50-fact line barely moves (0.983 -> 0.967 across the 3x cut) while the 800-fact line drops 0.650 -> 0.550 and flattens below 128. Scope is printed on the image itself: one encoder, one host, ollama 0.20.3, local fixture, not a benchmark.
